**Finding submitted: GOVLAW — deviation (preferred-level cure proposed).**

- **Governing law is fine.** Section 18.3 (p0765) already applies New York law, satisfying the first preferred element verbatim — no change proposed there.
- **The forum fails both levels.** Section 17.3 (p0744/p0747) sends every "Dispute" to *exclusive* final and binding ICC arbitration, and 17.3(a) (p0748) seats it in **Osaka, Japan** whenever Array demands. That is mandatory arbitration capable of being seated abroad — walk-away territory — and no court has merits jurisdiction; 17.3(g) preserves court access only for provisional relief, which does not cure the absence of a merits forum.
- **Smallest complete cure.** Three surgical replacements: retitle 17.3, strip the arbitration mandate from the chapeau, and substitute exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County over the merits with a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out. Because whole-paragraph deletion was rejected by the minimality gate, the residual tribunal machinery is switched off in place by one short sentence — expressly preserving Section 17.3(f) (internal-counsel privilege), which benefits us and contains no arbitration reference. The Section 17.2 Expert track is untouched.
